narrative_purpose: Lands the chapter's central inference in one glance: the same organ doing the same job comes out a different colour under a different sky, because the colour is set upstream by which photons arrive.
subject: A split-panel comparison of two leaves of identical shape and size, each on its own short stem. Left panel: a green leaf beneath a single pale yellow-white sun, with a soft wash of green light rising off its upper surface. Right panel: a deep violet leaf beneath two suns — a pale yellow-white one and a smaller dimmer orange one — with a soft wash of blue-violet light rising off its upper surface. The leaves are drawn as near-mirror twins so only colour and sky differ.
scene: Two paired specimen studies side by side against deep dark, divided by a thin vertical band of haze, each with its own small patch of sky above it.
camera: A straight-on paired study view, both leaves at identical size and angle for direct comparison.
light: Each leaf lit from its own sky above; the reflected wash above each leaf is the brightest element in its panel, and the two washes are clearly different colours.
palette: Void-indigo ground throughout; left leaf in muted living teal-green under a pale mist sun; right leaf in saturated violet and magenta under one pale sun and one restrained ember-amber companion; deep teal shadow around both.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, two specimens plated together for comparison.
detail_level: Crisp on both leaf blades and on the colour of the light washing off each; skies soft and hazy.
composition: Two equal vertical panels with a dark central seam, each leaf sitting in the lower half of its panel and its sky in the upper half, dark unbusy margins at the outer edges for overlaid callouts.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette overall; the left panel is permitted a slightly greener, more Earth-like cast so the contrast reads, but must not become warm or sunlit-photographic.
